gaps.sentence: You ___ pay for children under six — entry is free for them.
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' expresses absence of necessity: needn't pay.

gaps.sentence: You ___ take an umbrella — the forecast says heavy rain all day.
gaps.explanation: 'Should' recommends a sensible action: should take.

gaps.sentence: I really ___ stop drinking so much coffee; the doctor was very clear.
gaps.explanation: 'Must' can express strong obligation the speaker feels: must stop.

gaps.sentence: You ___ bring your own laptop — we will provide everything.
gaps.hint: no obligation, so needn't not mustn't
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' means it is not necessary; 'mustn't' would mean it is prohibited: needn't bring.

gaps.sentence: There ___ be a mistake — I ordered the vegetarian option.
gaps.explanation: 'Must' expresses the speaker's certainty about a present situation: must be.

gaps.sentence: We ___ book a table — the restaurant is never full on Mondays.
gaps.hint: the action is unnecessary, use needn't
gaps.explanation: When something is unnecessary, use 'needn't' or 'don't have to': needn't book.

gaps.sentence: He ___ not agree, but let us ask him anyway.
gaps.explanation: 'May' expresses a possibility about the future: may not agree.

gaps.sentence: Library books ___ be taken out of the reading room.
gaps.hint: a passive prohibition with mustn't be
gaps.explanation: Prohibitions can be passive: mustn't be taken.
